summary: Key inherited faḏ̣əl 'wundertätig (Heiligengrab)' to explicit I.2.
rationale: Its meaning is distinct from abundance/remaining and is independently confirmed by 44/121; existing wording is retained.

summary: New box Imperativ: example for sense 2 in Imperativ (Jan 1.8/185)

data.turoyo: Mərle: "D faḏḏal! (Mfaḏəl! Xlaṣ!)" Mərli: "La maʕ baʕəḏna tə nəmši, (Lo, ʕam ḥḏoḏe gəd mhalxina)."
data.translation: He said, 'Please, go ahead! (Please! Go on!)' I said, 'No, let us walk together. (No, we will walk together.)'

rationale: First native II Imperativ example, explicitly distinguished from the Arabic D faḏḏal in the source’s Turoyo parenthesis; the reply supplies going-together context. Supplied project machine translation [MT], not an edition translation.

summary: New sense 2: wundertätig (Heiligengrab, Wallfahrtsort)
rationale: Miracle-working is already glossed under Part act. but absent from the numbered sense list; 44/121 gives clear shrine predication. This makes an existing meaning explicit.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 1.1/47)

data.turoyo: w qəsəm mənayye d fuḏ̣elən, ksaymənne apšoṯo, kowən ann apšoṯanək basime.
data.translation: Die Trauben, die übrig bleiben, macht man zu Rosinen, es werden sehr wohl- schmeckende Rosinen.

rationale: Thin I Infectum cell; plural surplus-grape use confirms übrig bleiben beyond inherited food leftovers.

summary: example for sense 2 in Part act. (44/121)

data.turoyo: Kit harke zyara. W i zyaraṯe ġalabe faḏ̣əl yo.
data.translation: Hier gibt es einen Wallfahrtsort, und dieser Wallfahrtsort ist wundertätig.

rationale: Contextual attestation for explicit sense 2, replacing the isolation of a bare participial form with an intelligible shrine predication.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (Jan 1.36/1501)

data.turoyo: Qayəm ḥḏo amarikaniye mšayaʕla kallat xəṣuṣi w səmme u darbawo, b kallat di amarikaniyayo. W faḏəl stene, hən m Ḥanne w bəṯər mkamalle u darbawo. Amma aṣfalt lə səmme. Səmme, darbo aṣfalt lə səmme.
data.translation: Then an American woman sent money especially for it, and they made that road with that American woman's money. And some was left over too, some of that, and afterwards they completed that road. But they did not make it asphalt. They made it, they did not make an asphalt road.

rationale: Thin Preterit Intransitive I.1 cell; leftover funds support the round-1 übrig bleiben gloss. Source unmarked ḏ and opaque hən m Ḥanne are retained. Supplied project machine translation [MT], not an edition translation.

summary: Correct the object case: niemandem → niemanden
rationale: In 'jemanden jemandem vorziehen', the person preferred is accusative. Here 'mir' already supplies the dative. The supplied edition reads 'daß du niemanden mir vorziehst'.

summary: Sense 1: revise the gloss
rationale: Add the residual meaning already required by the inherited food-leftover example 69/197 and independently supported by surplus grapes. Abundance remains included.

summary: Sense 2: revise the gloss
before: (vom arabischen Imperativ tfaḏ̣ḏ̣al (bitte schön) hereinbitten durch tfaḏ̣ḏ̣al sagen;
after: (vom arabischen Imperativ tfaḏ̣ḏ̣al (bitte schön) hereinbitten durch tfaḏ̣ḏ̣al sagen; auch: höflich zum Vorausgehen auffordern
rationale: The explicitly Turoyo Mfaḏəl paraphrase invites the addressee to go ahead during a journey, not to enter a house. Widen only the invited action; retain the inherited formula explanation.

summary: I.1 is widened only to include übrig bleiben, a meaning already required by its own 69/197 example; no inherited terminology is modernized.
I.2 makes the already documented miracle-working Part act. meaning explicit. Predicative faḏ̣əl yo is attached to a shrine; no finite miracle-working paradigm is inferred.

The Arabic courtesy formula tfaḏ̣ḏ̣al, plural tfaḏ̣ḏ̣alu, is already in Idiomatic phrases. Contexts invite entry, speech, acceptance of an offer or attention. No new idiom or productive native Imperativ box is needed.

Native II.2 mfaḏ̣annole at 95/111 means inviting someone by saying the formula. It differs from uttering the borrowed formula itself. Occurrence decisions keep the latter in Idiomatic phrases, with no invented native stem assignment.
Formula uses include plural invitations at 53/76 and 90/57, and tfaḏ̣ḏ̣əl spellings at 111/56–75. These attest contact and local phonetic variants, not a native stem V.
57/216 lacks a corresponding German rendering of its final Tfaḏ̣ḏ̣al; no absent translation is supplied. No new light-verb collocation is required.

Round 2 only. Jan Beṯ-Şawoce English is project machine translation [MT]; readings rest on the supplied Turoyo. Existing and round-1 wording and numbering are retained. No edition translation is inferred.
Round 1 had already added I.2 miracle-working and widened I.1 to remaining. Jan does not add another sense under I.
Code-switching is explicit: Arabic D faḏḏal is followed by Turoyo Mfaḏəl in parentheses. This supplies native Imperativ evidence without treating the Arabic formula itself as a new stem.
Mafrəḏole is retained verbatim in its occurrence decision and editor question. No speculative transposition correction is applied to the entry or source, and no II Preterit box is published from it.
44/121: confirm agreement of masculine faḏ̣əl yo with the shrine expression i zyaraṯe; preserve the source spelling.
Should the Arabic formula's plural and invited-action variants be added to the existing Idiomatic phrases record? They are not native II inflections.
57/216: verify the omitted German rendering of the final formula before adding that quotation.
Confirm Mafrəḏole at Jan 2.12/2820: is it an error/metathesis for a preference form, or another lexeme? The fḏ̣l attribution and exact suffix roles remain provisional.
At Jan 1.36/1501, what does hən m Ḥanne resume? The leftover-funds reading is contextual; no source word is silently changed.
Jan examples have project machine translations [MT], not edition translations. Editors should check these English renderings against the Turoyo before treating them as vetted translations.
Leftover funds support the round-1 residual meaning in Preterit Intransitive; no additional surplus sense is proposed.
The native II imperative offers precedence on a path; the Arabic source formula remains separate from the Turoyo mfaḏəl paraphrase.
